findings: The November base capture retains the mobile collection and later charge purpose and presents three links for the same iOS, Android and React Native variants that had detailed inline bodies in the April 23, 2026 capture (new raw 5–15, old raw 1–10, 333–335 and 627–629). The bodies at those November links were not read. The diff at line 930 joins the deleted ending and the added iOS link. Their identity and scope are clear in the separately read raw files.

The April bodies separate client PaymentMethod creation and sending its ID, server attachment to a new or existing Customers v1 Customer, and the later PaymentIntent attempt. PaymentMethod listing uses `customer` or Accounts v2 `customer_account`; the attached-card and charge examples use `customer`. The paired April capture does not provide a complete Accounts v2 variant of those examples (old raw 118–229, 416–541 and 716–857).

The existing source lines 19–34 and 46–80 have the main flow, separate optional CVC client-confirm route and the Radar warning. It leaves out the consequential `requires_action`-to-decline behavior, response and recovery, and the upgrade route for authentication (source lines 13–34, old raw 211–233, 257–264 and 327–331). This matters if a maintainer queries what happens when an issuer requests authentication and implements a no-action flow expecting subsequent authentication or completion.

The November Attach PaymentMethod API reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-methods-attach-2026-11-07.md:5-11`) recommends a SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage` for future payments, and warns direct attachment alone does not optimize the method for future use. Preserve the dated April direct-attach path (old raw 150–183), but distinguish storage/association from optimized setup and eventual payment. The separate November Create PaymentIntent reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:432-450`) also says this `error_on_requires_action` flag needs `confirm=true` and fails the attempt if the intent transitions to `requires_action`.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Date the detailed platform bodies to 2026-04-23 (old raw 1–4). Keep SDK examples and compatibility in their dated platform scope, including iOS 13+ statement (44–54), Android SDK example 23.5.0 (369–396), React Native initialization (659–715), and test/live key and sandbox distinctions (116, 257–264, 414, 568–576, 714, 884–892).

Preserve customer opt-in and a record of written agreement for saving and future use. Offline-charge terms cover who initiates payments, timing/frequency, how amounts are determined, and the subscription cancellation policy where applicable. Retain the merchant's obligation to comply with applicable laws and network rules (old raw 14–25).

The dated simpler server-confirm path fails the attempt if authentication is required. The guide describes HTTP 402 and inspection of the error or PaymentIntent decline code, notifying the customer and recovering or upgrading to the integration that handles actions. The acquire, attach and charge operations must be kept distinct (old raw 118–233, 257–264 and 327–331).

Optional CVC re-collection is a separate client-confirm path using a server-created PaymentIntent, customer-associated saved method and platform SDK. The April guide says a payment might succeed even if CVC verification fails and points to Radar rules to block such payments (old raw 266–327, 578–621, 894–929).
conflicts: The dated April guide describes a simpler option for merchants that primarily do business in the US and Canada, and rejects it in countries requiring authentication to save cards, with India as an example (old raw 12–25, 337–350, 631–644). The mapped source line 13 and reciprocal routes in the Stripe index line 128 and concepts `stripe-inapp-payments.md:114` and `stripe-saved-payment-methods.md:157` broaden this to an exclusive US/Canada product eligibility claim. Preserve the April positioning and authentication/compliance conditions as dated, without carrying forward an all-card guarantee within the US or Canada or a fresh legal conclusion.

Mapped source lines 13 and 22–34 connect later charging with a historical `setup_future_usage: 'on_session'` charge-and-save example. Keep that example gated on an existing Customer and scope it to intended future use with the customer present (old raw 235–254). The separate November PaymentIntent Create reference (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:635-639,672-685`) distinguishes `on_session` and `off_session` future-use values from the attempted charge's `off_session` flag. The November migration guide gives the same on/off distinction for planned future charges (`raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-migration-2026-11-07.md:127-139`). Add reciprocal scope with the in-app concept's charge-and-save section (42–54) and the saved payment methods concept's off-session guidance (111–121); the April example does not establish suitability for unattended reuse.

source_assessments.reason: The November base change is navigation only. The existing summary can mislead readers about eligibility, future-use setup, and what the server does when the issuer requires authentication.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-card-without-authentication establishes the purpose of collecting card details in a mobile app for later charging and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The April 23, 2026 guide presents the simpler route for businesses primarily in the US and Canada, calls for opt-in and written agreement for future use, and warns that it is unsuitable where saving cards requires authentication, such as India (old raw lines 12-25). The client creates a PaymentMethod and sends its ID. The server associates it with a new or existing Customer, then separately creates and confirms a PaymentIntent using the saved method. Listing distinguishes Customers v1 `customer` from Accounts v2 `customer_account` (old raw lines 118-227). `error_on_requires_action: true` with `confirm: true` fails the payment attempt if customer action is required. The April guide describes HTTP 402, inspecting the decline, and customer recovery or upgrading the integration (old raw lines 211-233 and old raw lines 327-331). source-stripe-inapp-save-card-without-auth.md captures key steps, combined charge-and-save and optional CVC collection, but states a narrower country rule and leaves out this authentication failure boundary.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-card-without-authentication, the November capture moves the same three platform variants to a navigation index (new raw lines 9-15) without documenting fresh behavior or deprecation. source-stripe-inapp-save-card-without-auth.md and its reciprocal concept and index routes should date the April guide's regional positioning, eligibility conditions and consent, decline, UI and SDK details (old raw lines 12-54, old raw lines 211-264 and old raw lines 369-396). Retain the April simpler-integration example with an existing Customer and `setup_future_usage: 'on_session'` (old raw lines 235-254). The separate November Create PaymentIntent capture scopes `on_session` to future reuse with the customer present and distinguishes intended future use from the current charge's `off_session` flag (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:635-639,672-685`). The November Attach PaymentMethod reference explains that attachment alone lacks future-use optimization and recommends SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage` (`raw/stripe-api-payment-methods-attach-2026-11-07.md:5-11`). Preserve those boundaries in the in-app and saved payment methods concept routes so the old example is not taken as authority for unattended or optimized future charging. CVC re-collection uses a separate client confirmation path, and successful payment can coexist with a failed CVC check unless appropriate Radar blocking is configured (old raw lines 266-331 and old raw lines 894-929). The captures document these conditions and examples without proving a successful actual charge, account eligibility or compliance.
